title: Model-Route latency portrait with IO-mode split and trace hook integration
creator: Aisha Campos
description:
Goal: Ship a set of Grafana dashboards and underlying metric/log pipeline changes that surface per-model, per-route latency distributions (p50/p95/p99) with an explicit split for streaming vs non-streaming IO modes, and direct trace links from dashboard panels into the tracing system. This ticket covers metric design, telemetry pipeline changes (Prometheus/OTLP + trace hooks), dashboard layout, and rollout plan.

Scope and success criteria:
- Panels that show p50/p95/p99 latency for each model-route combination and allow filtering by route tags, model version, and region.
- Side-by-side breakdown for streaming vs non-streaming requests (streaming lines and non-streaming bars by percentile).
- Heatmap view for model x route p95 over last 90 days with anomaly markers.
- Dashboard panels include clickable links to correlated traces (span id / trace id) for sampled requests.
- Backfill of derived metrics for the last 30 days for historical comparisons.
- Alerts based on p95 breach and sudden delta between streaming and non-streaming p95.

Telemetry design decisions:
- Use histogram metrics (prometheus histograms + OTLP histograms) for accurate percentile computation at the aggregation layer instead of relying on client-side summary percentiles.
- Define standardized buckets tailored to observed latencies: [1ms, 5ms, 10ms, 25ms, 50ms, 100ms, 250ms, 500ms, 1s, 2s, 5s, 10s]. Buckets chosen to capture tail behavior without exploding cardinality.
- Emit labels: service=model-serving, model_name, model_version, route, io_mode (streaming|sync), region, cpu_arch, quantization_profile (if present). Keep label set minimal to avoid high-cardinality.
- Sampling: Traces sampled at 1% global; increase to 5% for requests with latency > p95 threshold to ensure trace availability for tail analysis. Implement dynamic sampling via trace-sampler component.

Pipeline changes required:
- Instrument runtime to emit OTLP histograms for request latency and to attach trace_id/span_id into logs/metrics where available. Runtime PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1482.
- Add a lightweight pre-processing job in the metrics pipeline to convert incoming histograms to aggregated percentiles for dashboards to avoid expensive on-the-fly histogram math in Grafana. (See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Histogram+Aggregation+Design).
- Ensure logs include structured fields route and model identifiers so linking from dashboard -> logs -> traces is reliable.

Trade-offs considered and decisions made:
- Summary metrics vs histograms: Chosen histograms due to accuracy for p99. The trade-off is slightly increased ingestion cost and storage; mitigated by controlled bucket choices and label pruning.
- Full trace capture vs sampling: Full capture is cost-prohibitive. We use adaptive sampling (global low rate, upsample tail) to keep costs reasonable while preserving troubleshooting signal.
- Per-model-cardinality: Avoid emitting per-deployment heavy labels (customer_id) in the metric path; instead use logs/trace annotations for customer-specific drilldowns to reduce cardinality in metrics indices.

Rollout plan:
1) Instrumentation PRs in runtime + SDK (staging): runtime/pull/1482 and sdk-js/pull/572.
2) Deploy histogram ingestion and aggregation job to metrics staging cluster.
3) Deploy dashboard to staging, run backfill for 30 days.
4) Run smoke tests and verify trace linking.
5) Gradual production cutover behind feature flag (2 weeks), monitor ingestion cost and panel latency.

Success metrics:
- Dashboards show expected percentiles with <5% error vs ad-hoc offline calculations.
- Trace links resolve for >90% of sampled tail requests.
- Read-only dashboard panel load time < 3s for common queries.
- No more than 15% increase in ingestion storage after label pruning and bucket tuning.
